legend: The cellular components of pituitary blastomas include large adenohypophysial neuroendocrine cells arranged in lobules or diffuse sheets, cuboidal primitive Rathke pouch epithelium with rosette or gland/follicle formation, and scattered undifferentiated blastemal cells.

The adenohypophysial neuroendocrine tumour cells are arranged in diffuse sheets or lobules and are variably positive for ACTH. Unlike the cells arranged in sheets, rosette- or follicle-forming cuboidal or columnar primitive Rathke pouch epithelium and blastemal undifferentiated cells tend to be negative for ACTH.
CAM5.2 (low-molecular-weight cytokeratin) immunohistochemistry stains almost all cellular components in pituitary blastomas.
Strong membranous CD56 expression distinguishes areas of neuroendocrine cells, whereas other cellular elements show reduced staining intensity for CD56.
EMA shows variable staining in cellular components, with stronger staining in areas with rosette- or follicle-forming cuboidal or columnar primitive Rathke pouch epithelium.
S100 stains scattered folliculostellate cells in a pituitary blastoma.

Proliferative heterogeneity of the various cellular components. The follicle-forming cuboidal or columnar primitive Rathke pouch epithelium shows a higher Ki-67 proliferation index than other cellular elements.
ACTH-positive neuroendocrine cells show reduced nuclear p27 expression, as seen in most functioning corticotroph tumours.
source: Contributors for this illustration include Ozgur Mete, Leanne de Kock and William D. Foulkes

legend: From DICER1 mutation to tumorigenesis. Each tumour starts with presumptively biallelic mutations in DICER1 (RNase IIIb hotspot mutation coupled with a loss-of-function variant [LOF] or loss of heterozygosity [LOH]). Because the RNase IIIa domain of DICER1 remains functional, the processing of microRNA precursors (pre-miRNAs) will generate a skewed distribution of 5p/3p mature microRNA; as shown in the graphic, this improper dicing of precursors results in aberrant 5p products and a skewed distribution of microRNAs favouring 3p over 5p microRNAs. This in turn leads to the dysregulation of hundreds of 5p and 3p microRNAs, with the concomitant dysregulation of many target mRNAs. In the case of pituitary blastoma (PitB), this includes the upregulation of PRAME (fold-change: > 500). Gene-set analyses showed that the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) pathway and the WNT, NOTCH, and PI3K pathways are activated in pituitary blastoma tumours, as compared with normal postnatal pituitary (NPP) samples. The analysis revealed that, like normal fetal pituitary (NFP), PitB samples have a high level of undifferentiated cells as compared with NPP samples. PitB tumours have the lowest level of differentiated cells, as compared with NPP and NFP samples. Pink represents upregulated processes and blue represents a downregulated process.
